extractedFieldMetaData.fieldDescription: The type of unit being rented (e.g., studio, 1-bedroom, office space).
The total number of residential units accounted for in the rent roll, representing all leasable spaces within the property.
The average size of a residential unit, calculated by dividing the total space size by the assigned number of units.
The combined total size of all residential units in the property, typically measured in square feet or meters.
The measurement unit used for specifying the size of residential spaces, such as square feet (SF) or square meters (m²).
The market rent rate for a unit.
The average rent amount per unit size (e.g., per square foot).
The initial rent amount agreed upon in the lease, not including additional expenses.

Refers to the average rental amount charged per unit or space, excluding additional charges such as utilities, maintenance fees, or other expenses. It is typically calculated by dividing the total base rent by the number of rented units or spaces.
The number of units currently occupied by tenants.
The number of units that are available for lease.
The number of units that are currently vacant.
The percentage of units that are currently occupied.
The percentage of units that are currently vacant.
The combined total size of all residential units in the property, typically measured in square feet or meters.
The average size of all spaces or units in a property, calculated by dividing the total space size by the total number of units. This provides a measure of the typical unit size within the property.
The aggregate rental value that could be achieved if all units were leased at current market rates. It represents the total potential income based on prevailing market conditions.
The average rent amount per unit size (e.g., per square foot).
The sum of all charges under active leases, including base rent and any additional fees outlined in the lease agreements.
The average amount charged per unit or space under active leases, calculated by dividing the total lease charges by the number of leased units.
The total count of residential or commercial units available within a property, regardless of their occupancy status.
The proportion of units currently leased or occupied in relation to the total number of units, typically expressed as a percentage.
Specify the total acutal rental amount for occupied units. (Usually found in summary table under charge code named as rent, affrent)
Specify the total acutal average rental amount for occupied units.
The name or identifier of the asset/property being rented.

Indicates the specific time frame that the documents data represents, covering the start and end dates relevant to the information contained within, such as financial, operational, or contractual details.
The total count of residential or commercial units available within a property, regardless of their occupancy status.
Complete amount paid by the tenant for the lease of a property, typically including both base rent and any additional charges specified in the lease agreement.
The number of units that are currently vacant.
The number of units that are available for lease.
The average rent across all units, calculated by dividing the total rent collected by the total number of units, including both occupied and vacant units.
The proportion of units currently leased or occupied in relation to the total number of units, typically expressed as a percentage.
